evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 9.94 mg/L, ~5x the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P(48h)=2.89 g/L, within source-batch range 2.98-3.06 g/L
Receiving DO2 trajectory parallels source-1/2/3 (26-28 h dip with full recovery to 10.5-11.5 mg/L)
Product rising steeply (1.0 -> 2.9 g/L between 36 h and 48 h assays), indicating healthy production
args.rationale: The receiving batch tracks the three source batches within normal batch-to-batch variability: DO2 ~9.9 mg/L at 52 h (far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, trajectory analogous to sources), and product P(48h)=2.89 g/L matches the source range (2.98-3.06 g/L). There is no oxygen stress, no growth/product deficit, and no anomalous state, so no intervention is needed; feed reduction or aeration changes would risk product mass for no benefit, and stop yields zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: Receiving DO2 runs ~0.5-1.5 mg/L below source levels in later hours; if this widening continued it could indicate mild OTR deficit, but the margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint is large. Product assay is 4 h delayed, so current P is extrapolated from the 48 h value. Hidden receiving parameters could differ from source; forward-model predictions were not needed given healthy margins, adding modest residual uncertainty.
